result.topic_en: Euler completes a finite expression for a double series in terms of the zeta-type sums $\int \frac{1}{z^k}$ and partial sums $1+\frac{1}{2^k}+\dots+\frac{1}{a^k}$, then in §8 sums over all values of $a$ to obtain an expression in products of such sums.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 147
$\pm \frac{1}{a^m}\int\frac{1}{z^n} \pm \frac{m}{1.a^{m+1}}\int\frac{1}{z^{n-1}} \pm \frac{m(m+1)}{1.2\,a^{m+2}}\int\frac{1}{z^{n-2}}$
$\pm \frac{m(m+)(m+2)}{1.2.3\,a^{m+3}}\int\frac{1}{z^{n-3}} \pm \text{etc.}$
$\mp \frac{1}{a^m}\left(1+\frac{1}{2^n}+\frac{1}{3^n}+\dots\dots+\frac{1}{a^n}\right)$
$\mp \frac{m}{1\,a^{m+1}}\left(1+\frac{1}{2^{n-1}}+\frac{1}{3^{n-1}}+\dots+\frac{1}{a^{n-1}}\right)$
$\mp \frac{m(m+1)}{1.2\,a^{m+2}}\left(1+\frac{1}{2^{u-2}}+\frac{1}{3^{n-2}}+\dots+\frac{1}{a^{n-2}}\right)$
$\mp \frac{m(m+1)(m+2)}{1.2.3\,a^{m+3}}\left(1+\frac{1}{2^{m-3}}+\frac{1}{3^{n-3}}+\dots+\frac{1}{a^{n-3}}\right.$
etc.
vbi signis superioribus eſt vtendum, quoties $m$ eſt numerus par, contra vero inferioribus. Expreſſio autem haec ſemper eſt finita, quoniam vtrumque terminorum ordinem tantum vsque ad $\int\frac{1}{z}$ continuari conuenit.

8. Tribuantur iam quoque litterae $a$ omnes valores ab vnitate in infinitum, vt in vna ſumma conplectamur omnes ſeries infinitas prioris ordinis §. 5. ad ſiniſtram notatas; atque earum ſumma ita reperietur repraeſentata:
$\int\frac{1}{z^n}.\int\frac{1}{z^m} - \frac{n}{1}\int\frac{1}{z^{n+1}}\int\frac{1}{z^{m-1}} + \frac{n(n+1)}{1.2}\int\frac{1}{z^{n+2}}.\int\frac{1}{z^{m-2}}$
$-\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1.\ 2.\ 3.}\int\frac{1}{z^{n+3}}.\int\frac{1}{z^{m-3}}$ etc.
T 2 $\pm$

items.quote: Expreſſio autem haec ſemper eſt finita, quoniam vtrumque terminorum ordinem tantum vsque ad $\int\frac{1}{z}$ continuari conuenit.
items.english: This expression is always finite, since each order of terms is to be continued only as far as $\int\frac{1}{z}$.

items.quote: atque earum ſumma ita reperietur repraeſentata:
items.english: and their sum will be found represented thus (by the series of products of $\int 1/z^k$ terms).
